chunk_findings.detail: `_strip_continuations` walks double quotes by stopping at the next raw `"`, so a `"` that bash opens inside a `$(...)` (or backtick) nested in that quote is treated as the closer, and the real closer later re-opens a quote that swallows the rest of the line. Given `echo "$(echo "x")"; git push origin main`, bash prints `x` and then runs `git push`; after the strip the text is one quoted word (`echo "$(echo "x)"; git push origin main` with the quote never closed), `_scan` never sees a command-separating `;`, and the push is not refused. `_dquote_end` already recurses into `$(` / backticks, but every caller strips first, so that logic never sees the original spans.
